answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes. Tending a quartz, watching a ridge, and naming a vault is the rhythm of earning trust — deliberately, repeatably, and never in bulk.
